title: Why Do Markets Exist?
hook: Before you try to beat the market, understand what the market is doing.

launchpad.outcome: Explain why markets exist, and why disagreement between buyers and sellers is what creates a transaction, not a problem.
launchpad.missionQuestion: If two traders disagree about where price is headed, can they still both trade at the same price?

slides.body: Participants enter markets for different reasons: some speculate, some hedge risk, some invest or manage portfolios. Price helps buyers and sellers find where they're willing to transact, and as that willingness changes, price changes too.

check.prompt: A new trader assumes every single person in the futures market is trying to speculate on which way price will go.

options.label: That's true
options.body: Everyone in the market is speculating on direction.
options.feedback: Not quite. Plenty of participants are managing risk exposure, not betting on direction.

options.label: Not necessarily
options.body: Some participants, like producers, hedge and manage risk instead.
options.why: Right: same market, different objective. Hedgers and speculators can both be on the other side of your trade.

slides.title: Why two people can both be right to trade

items.label: A seller shows up
items.desc: "I'm willing to sell here." Doesn't matter why.

items.label: Neither is wrong
items.desc: They just want different things at the same price.

slides.quote: The chart you're eventually going to analyze is simply the visual record of all that buying and selling activity. That's why we're going to spend so much time learning how to read price.

slides.body: Trader A believes the current price is an attractive buy. Trader B believes price is likely to fall and wants to sell, at the exact same price.

check.prompt: Can they both participate in the same market at the same time?

options.label: No
options.body: The market would reject one of their orders.
options.feedback: Markets don't reject orders based on who turns out to be right later.

options.label: Yes
options.body: Their disagreement is exactly what creates the transaction.
options.why: Disagreement between participants isn't a glitch. It's the entire reason a transaction can happen at all.

options.label: No
options.body: Only one of them can be right, so only one can trade.
options.feedback: Being "right" isn't a requirement to trade, willingness to transact is.

slides.prompt: Why is disagreement between market participants necessary for trading to occur? Explain it in your own words.
slides.modelAnswer: If everyone agreed on where price should be, no one would want to trade with anyone else. A buyer needs someone willing to sell, and a seller needs someone willing to buy. That disagreement is literally what creates a transaction. No disagreement means no trade.

takeaways: Markets exist because participants with different needs transact.
Some participants speculate, others hedge risk: same market, different objective.
Disagreement between buyers and sellers is what creates a transaction, not a problem with the market.
remember: The chart is just the visual record of buyers and sellers disagreeing.
